title: run_command: PowerShell -Command quoting fails through cmd.exe on Windows
description: On Windows, run_command executes via cmd.exe. When the command string contains a double-quoted -Command argument (e.g. powershell -Command "Write-Output hello"), cmd.exe's quote parser interferes: the inner command string is echoed to stdout rather than executed, with exit code 0. The failure is silent — no stderr, no non-zero exit code, no error result. Discovered in run e525860c when attempting to append rows to the signal index via PowerShell. Workaround: write a .ps1 temp file and invoke with powershell -File, which bypasses cmd.exe quote parsing.
proposed_resolution: Fix run_command on Windows to invoke PowerShell via a temp script file (powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File <tmpfile>) rather than -Command "..." when the command targets PowerShell, eliminating cmd.exe quote interference. Alternatively, document in the skill that agents must use the -File pattern for multi-statement PowerShell on Windows.
